title: Cell death-associated genes as novel diagnostic biomarkers for autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Li, Chanhua; Wei, Lijuan; Chen, Wanling; Ran, Guanghui; Liu, Lili; Li, Zhongyi; Song, Anhua; Liu, Meiliang; Huang, Dongping; Tang, Kun; Zeng, Xiaoyun; Wang, Lijun
journal: Apoptosis : an international journal on programmed cell death
one_liner_zh: 该研究利用机器学习构建自闭症诊断模型，虽涉及转录因子预测但核心为基因表达诊断标志物，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或机制研究，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) involves neuroinflammation and dysregulated neuronal death but lacks objective diagnostic biomarkers. This study investigated whether cell death could serve as a molecular basis for ASD diagnosis. We identified cell death-associated genes (CDGs) in peripheral blood mononuclear cells between ASD and control groups and performed functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction, immune characteristics, and non-negative matrix factorization clustering analyses. Key genes were further selected using 6 machine learning algorithms and weighted gene co-expression network analysis to construct a diagnostic model, which was subsequently validated using external human blood samples and mice prefrontal cortex samples. We explored microRNAs (miRNAs), transcription factors (TFs), and drugs potentially interacted with the key genes. Fourteen CDGs and 4 out of 22 types of immune cells were differentially expressed between ASD and controls in GSE18123. These genes were enriched in pathways such as neuron apoptosis and RAGE receptor binding. Among 6 machine learning models, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) model exhibited the best performance. Six key genes were selected as the most important hub genes and used to construct the diagnostic model. The model showed AUCs of 0.722 in GSE42133, 0.781 in our local samples, and 0.889 in mice prefrontal cortex samples. A total of 172 miRNAs, 111 TFs, and 98 drugs were found to interact with these key genes. The expression patterns of CDGs in the peripheral blood of children with ASD demonstrate potential diagnostic value. Further studies are warranted to validate their diagnostic performance in real-world settings and to elucidate the role of cell death dysregulation in ASD.
abstract_zh: 自闭症谱系障碍（ASD）涉及神经炎症和神经元死亡失调，但缺乏客观的诊断生物标志物。本研究探讨了细胞死亡是否可作为ASD诊断的分子基础。我们在ASD组与对照组之间鉴定了外周血单核细胞中的细胞死亡相关基因（CDGs），并进行了功能富集、蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用、免疫特征及非负矩阵分解聚类分析。通过6种机器学习算法和加权基因共表达网络分析进一步筛选关键基因以构建诊断模型，并随后使用外部人类血液样本和小鼠前额叶皮层样本进行验证。我们探索了与关键基因可能相互作用的微小RNA（miRNAs）、转录因子（TFs）及药物。在GSE18123中，ASD与对照组之间共有14个CDGs和22种免疫细胞中的4种差异表达。这些基因富集于神经元凋亡和RAGE受体结合等通路。在6种机器学习模型中，K-最近邻（KNN）模型表现最佳。筛选出6个关键基因作为最重要的枢纽基因，并用于构建诊断模型。该模型在GSE42133中的AUC为0.722，在我们本地样本中为0.781，在小鼠前额叶皮层样本中为0.889。共发现172个miRNAs、111个TFs和98种药物与这些关键基因相互作用。ASD儿童外周血中CDGs的表达模式显示出潜在的诊断价值。需进一步研究以验证其在真实世界环境中的诊断性能，并阐明细胞死亡失调在ASD中的作用。
